$comment: Single source of truth for the CrossMetric Priority for Review model. Read by the Python pipeline (pipeline/scoring/model.py) and the TypeScript engine (packages/engine/src/model.ts). Changing any number here requires a version bump and a CHANGELOG entry in docs/METHODOLOGY.md.
name: CrossMetric Priority for Review

normalization.population: All candidate locations inside the selected school's analysis radius.
normalization.formula: score(v) = 100 * (number of candidates with value <= v) / N
normalization.zeroEvidenceRule: For evidence components, a candidate with zero matching crashes scores 0. Absence of observed crashes contributes no priority, rather than the percentile of a large tie at zero.
normalization.reference: OECD/JRC (2008), Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators, sections 5 (normalisation) and 6 (weighting).

components.label: Crash Evidence
components.description: Number of reported crashes matched to this location in the analysis period (after the crash filter).

components.label: Injury Evidence
components.description: Matched crashes with at least one reported injury or fatality.

components.label: Pedestrian Evidence
components.description: Matched crashes in which a recorded unit was a pedestrian.

components.label: Traffic Context
components.description: GDOT Annual Average Daily Traffic: vehicles passing a mid-block location, or the sum of the crossing roads' AADT at an intersection.

components.label: School Proximity
components.description: Straight-line distance from the school's NCES location to the nearest point of the candidate.

scenarios.label: Standard (Balanced)
scenarios.description: Equal weights. With no empirical basis for ranking one indicator above another, equal weighting is the transparent default.

scenarios.label: Pedestrian emphasis
scenarios.description: Doubles the weight of pedestrian-involved crash evidence.

scenarios.label: Injury emphasis
scenarios.description: Doubles the weight of injury and fatal crash evidence.

scenarios.label: Crash-history emphasis
scenarios.description: Doubles the weight of total crash evidence.

scenarioRationale: Emphasis scenarios are not claims about which indicator matters most. They are deliberate, declared perturbations of the Standard weights, used to test whether a location's priority depends on one assumption (sensitivity analysis).

combination.formula: priority = sum(w_i * s_i) / sum(w_i), over components with available data
combination.rounding: Scores are kept at full precision for ranking and displayed rounded to the nearest integer.

stability.definition: spread = (worst rank) - (best rank) across all scenarios. Stability is High when spread <= max(2, 10% of N), Moderate when spread <= max(4, 25% of N), otherwise Low. N = candidates in the analysis.

planner.definition: When filling review slots in priority order, a candidate is skipped if it lies within coverageRadiusM of an already-selected location on a shared road, because one professional review would naturally cover both.

periodRationale: GDOT's public crash layer is a rolling window of roughly three years, so a five-year period is not offered. The window ends on the last month GDOT has fully loaded.
